packages.title: Kling 4.0 in the cloud: 3-30 s takes, multi-shot, references and video edit, now that fal's API is open
packages.brief:
WHY. Kling 4.0 is the flagship closed video model of the month (Higgsfield has offered it since 2026-10-21). Round 4 recorded its four fal endpoints but held them back as 'playground-only'. On 2026-11-01 the llms.txt pages for kling/v4/text-to-video and kling/v4/video-to-video/edit document live fal.run endpoints with no 'coming soon', and Replicate lists kwaivgi/kling-v4.0. It is the cheapest big win: catalog work only.
WHERE IT SHOWS UP. Video studio model menu (Best list), Cinema Studio takes (multi-shot up to 30 s, @Elements), Edit video (Kling 4 edit), Genjutsu Swap / Insert model picker, Assist and MCP model lists.
Research record: docs/research/paid-model-apis-4.json already holds kling/v4/text-to-video, image-to-video, reference-to-video and video-to-video/edit with status 'playground-only' (catalog date 2026-10-16) and a recommendation not to route until the page drops "API access is coming soon". On 2026-11-01 https://fal.ai/models/kling/v4/text-to-video/llms.txt and .../video-to-video/edit/llms.txt describe live endpoints (fal.run, Key auth) with no waitlist (docs/research/new-models-10.md §2.2). FIRST re-fetch all four OpenAPI schemas with the existing scripts (the same way round 4 did) and confirm image-to-video and reference-to-video are live too; flip each record's status to active only if its page is live, and note the date. Replicate: replicate.com/explore lists kwaivgi/kling-v4.0 ("3-30 second videos up to 1080p and edits existing videos"): fetch its schema and add it as a second provider only if its inputs map cleanly.
START by mapping what already exists against the plan: earlier packages built parts of this (read git log --oneline on the base for the files the plan names, the catalog, the studio code and its tests). Build only the gaps, extend what exists rather than duplicating it, and say in your report which plan items were already there.
Facts to build on (from the fal pages; re-check): text-to-video takes prompt OR multi_prompt (a list of shots whose durations sum to the total), duration 3-30 s (default 5), resolution 720p | 1080p (default 1080p), aspect_ratio 16:9 | 9:16 | 1:1 | 21:9; $0.157/s at 720p, $0.235/s at 1080p. image-to-video adds start_image_url (required) and end_image_url. reference-to-video takes image_urls, video_urls, elements, start_image_url, multi_prompt. video-to-video/edit takes prompt (the source is @Video1), video_url (3-30.05 s, <= 300 MB, 700-4553 px a side, aspect 0.40-2.50, 23.9-60.05 fps), image_urls (@Image1..), video_urls (up to 4, @Video2..; source + references + element videos <= 30 s in all), elements (up to 7; up to 3 with a voice_id, up to 3 video elements), voice_ids (up to 3, made with fal's create-voice model), duration 3-30, resolution; billed $0.094/s (720p) or $0.141/s (1080p) on input plus output seconds with a minimum of 2x the output. Kling's own spec (atlascloud summary of the release note) adds 10 keyframes, 15 mixed references, 10-bit HDR "coming soon" and 2-minute extension "coming soon": the fal API exposes none of the keyframe, HDR or extension features, so do not claim them.
Build:
1. scripts/gen-cloud-models.py: model("kling-4", "Kling 4.0", "Kuaishou", "kling", "video", ...) with routes t2v, i2v, flf2v (start + end image), ref2v (images, clips, @Elements) and v2v (edit), price per second by resolution, and the edit / clip-reference billing rule (input + output seconds, minimum 2x output) in the price function, never shown as the plain per-second rate. Regenerate src/lib/catalog/cloud-models.generated.ts (pnpm gen:catalog). Badges: top, 30s. Place it in the Video studio's Best list next to Seedance 2.5 and FLUX 3 Max.
2. Multi-shot: map Fuobe's shot list (Cinema multi-shot takes, the Video studio's multi-shot) to multi_prompt [{prompt, duration}], so a 30 s take is one call; keep the automatic extend for longer takes on models that need it.
3. Elements: Fuobe Elements @mentions become Kling elements (images, or a short clip for a video element); a voice element needs a fal voice id: if Fuobe has no fal create-voice flow, leave voices out and say so in the picker ("voices: not yet").
4. Edit video: Kling 4 edit as a model in Edit video and in Genjutsu's Swap / Insert pickers, with the 30 s and 300 MB limits checked before upload and the input-plus-output price shown first.
5. Frames mode stays on FLUX 3 Max keyframes (src/lib/catalog/keyframes.ts says Kling 4.0 takes 10 frames; the hosted API does not): fix that comment so it does not promise Kling keyframes.
6. Engine labels: Kling 4.0 is a closed model, so it is cloud-only like the other partner models; "Open source only" hides it. The open engine keeps its own models: nothing changes there.
7. Licence row: proprietary paid API (Kuaishou via fal / Replicate), switched on.
Tests: payload tests for each route against the stored schemas (multi_prompt durations sum, 21:9, 1080p default, start/end image, 4 reference videos, 7 elements), the price function (5 s at 720p = $0.785; a 10 s edit at 1080p bills max(input+output, 2x output) seconds), Cinema multi-shot mapping, the mock provider. Browser checks of the Video studio menu, a Cinema take and Edit video at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, in demo mode. No paid call can be made here: say so.
CLOUD ONLY WHERE IT IS HOSTED: a feature gets a cloud route only when the model itself (or its base model with LoRA support, for a LoRA) is hosted on fal or Replicate with the inputs it needs. If it isn't, the feature is on the open engine (ComfyUI) only: no substitute recipe on the cloud. The cloud engine says plainly that it runs on your GPU (open source), and Engine mode "Paid APIs only" hides or refuses it with that reason. EACH ENGINE DOES ALL IT CAN (since 10-30): the cloud uses only hosted models, with what the hosted endpoint supports; the open engine keeps every capability it has (LoRAs, custom nodes, longer clips, reference images) even when the cloud can't match it. Never remove or weaken a local capability because the cloud lacks it: a LoRA that only works locally runs locally, and the cloud runs the same hosted model without it. The UI says plainly what each engine does.
MAIN CHANGED THIS AREA (10-30): main's GPU pre-flight board (/connect; STUDIO_ROWS and the preset map in src/server/gpu/tools.ts; chips from /api/gpu/badges) shows every studio, app and model as Ready / One step away / Needs setup / Needs a bigger GPU. Give a new studio page, hub tool or app its row there, and make sure its ComfyUI graphs reach workflows/comfyui/requirements.json (the library build writes it; pin a new node pack in workflows/comfyui/packs.json and new model files in workflows/comfyui/model-pins.json).
PUBLIC SIGN-UP (the owner's, on main: docs/public-signup.md at your base, which wins where it says more than this; the accounts lane acc-* was dropped on 2026-10-30, and docs/research/accounts-8.md is background research only): every route, tool, page and run you add follows it the way main's own routes do. Read src/lib/guest-access.ts, src/proxy.ts, src/server/tenant.ts and tests/public-signup.test.ts first. Guests browse read-only (changes answer 401). Accounts see the owner's library as a guest does: the owner's lists come back empty (EMPTY_LISTS), other reads of them are refused, a change to the library or projects goes in LIBRARY_CHANGES (403 code library), and a visitor is never told whether one of the owner's records exists. Install-wide settings, keys and tokens stay the owner's (OWNER_WRITES, OWNER_ALL). Only the owner's runs reach the install's keys or GPU: an account runs studio generations through POST /api/generations on its own ComfyUI (onOwnGpu in src/server/providers/comfyui.ts; accountRun in src/server/generations.ts keeps chained steps the account's own); without a GPU any run answers connect-gpu, and a tool that plans with the studio's own AI helpers or keeps projects of its own answers own-gpu-tool (so does every 3D model for now). examples: A red fox standing in fresh snow at sunrise, its breath visible in the cold air. Soft golden light rakes across the snowfield from the left, pine forest softly blurred in the background, shot at eye level with a telephoto lens.

enable_prompt_expansion.desc: If set to true, the prompt is expanded into a detailed caption (grounded in the reference images when editing) before generation.

seed.desc: The same seed and the same prompt given to the same version of the model will output the same image every time.

num_images.desc: The number of images to generate.

enable_safety_checker.desc: If set to true, the safety checker will be enabled.

output_format.desc: The format of the generated image.

sync_mode.desc: If `True`, the media will be returned as a data URI and the output data won't be available in the request history.

width.desc: The width of the generated image.

height.desc: The height of the generated image.

image_size.desc: The size of the generated image. Each side can be 256 to 4096 pixels (native 4K).

y_max.desc: Bottom edge as a fraction of the image height (0-1).

x_max.desc: Right edge as a fraction of the image width (0-1).

x_min.desc: Left edge as a fraction of the image width (0-1).

y_min.desc: Top edge as a fraction of the image height (0-1).

label.desc: Short name for the object in this box, e.g. `fox`. Write `<fox>` in the prompt to tie the box to those words; a box the prompt doesn't name is added to the scene. Defaults to `obj_<n>`.

description.desc: What to draw in this box: the object and its look.
examples: a red fox with thick orange fur and a white-tipped tail

bounding_boxes.desc: Optional layout: draw each described object inside its box. Box edges are fractions of the image size, with (0, 0) at the top-left. Name boxes in the prompt by label, e.g. `A red fox <fox> sits under a red umbrella <umbrella>`.

prompt.desc: The text prompt describing the music to generate
examples: Mysterious original soundtrack, themes of jungle, rainforest, nature, woodwinds, busy rhythmic tribal percussion.

text.desc: The text to generate for this chunk. Can start with an optional section name in square brackets, e.g. [Verse 1], followed by lyric lines, plus inline directions in curly braces, e.g. {scratching}. Section names must be between 1 and 100 characters. At most 30 lines are allowed, each at most 200 characters.
examples:
[Verse 1]
Neon rain on empty streets
I keep walking to the beat

duration_ms.desc: The duration of the chunk in milliseconds. Must be between 3000ms and 120000ms.

negative_styles.desc: The styles and musical directions that should not be present in this chunk. Leaving this empty is a good default; only set it to explicitly avoid a particular style or direction.

positive_styles.desc: The styles and musical directions that should be present in this chunk. Use English for best results. The styles of the first chunk matter most as they set the overall tone and genre; later chunks can add nuance, progression or change direction.

context_adherence.desc: How closely this chunk follows the context of its surrounding chunks. Low adherence lets the model deviate and be more creative, high adherence keeps it consistent with the surrounding context.

start_ms.desc: Offset into the clip where the referenced window starts, in milliseconds.

strength.desc: How strongly the model follows the reference. Low lets it deviate and be more creative, high keeps it close to the reference.

end_ms.desc: Offset into the clip where the referenced window ends, in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000ms after start_ms, or the end of the clip if it is shorter. The window must be at most 30000ms long.

audio_url.desc: URL of the audio clip to use as the style reference.

audio_reference.desc: An audio clip whose style conditions this chunk. The reference on the first chunk matters most: it influences every later chunk, so condition from the first chunk to style the whole song.

chunks.desc: The chunks that make up the generation, in order. At most 30 chunks, totalling between 3000ms and 600000ms.

composition_plan.desc: The chunk-based composition plan for the music

music_length_ms.desc: The length of the song to generate in milliseconds. Used only in conjunction with prompt. Must be between 3000ms and 600000ms. Optional - if not provided, the model will choose a length based on the prompt.

force_instrumental.desc: If true, guarantees that the generated song will be instrumental. If false, the song may or may not be instrumental depending on the prompt. Can only be used with prompt.

seed.desc: Random seed to initialize the music generation process. Can only be used with composition_plan. The same seed with the same parameters gives more consistent results, but exact reproducibility is not guaranteed.

output_format.desc: Output format of the generated audio. Formatted as codec_sample_rate_bitrate. So an mp3 with 22.05kHz sample rate at 32kbs is represented as mp3_22050_32. Note that the μ-law format (sometimes written mu-law, often approximated as u-law) is commonly used for Twilio audio inputs.
